title: GGT–ALT coupling did not improve HbA1c classification beyond flexible additive laboratory predictors across two NHANES samples
abstract: A registered existing-data test evaluated a standardized log-GGT × log-ALT interaction beyond glucose, age, sex, BMI and flexible enzyme main effects. NHANES2007–08 discovery included5218 adults; separate2009–10 confirmation included5613. Weighted Brier gain (baseline minus candidate) was-0.000112 in source PSU-grouped cross-validation and-0.000117 in frozen confirmation. Target rescaled-PSU bootstrap95% interval was−0.000266 to+0.000013;300 source/target-refit interval was−0.000795 to+0.000171. Confirmation AUROC slightly decreased. A linear comparator gave a tiny positive gain, underscoring comparator dependence. This negative predictive result does not establish absent enzyme biology, causal effects or lack of other useful interactions. Separate survey samples are not external-program replication; unlinked repeat participation is unverifiable. Author arithmetic/leakage checks and offline clean rerun supplied; no independent peer review.
